extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, International Preliminary Examining Authorities, International Searching Authorities, national/elected Offices and International Bureau staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing the content, form, timing, transmission, translation, and handling of the international preliminary examination report (Chapter II PCT) and related communications between International Preliminary Examining Authorities, the International Bureau, elected Offices and applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for international preliminary examination (Rule 69.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time limit for establishing the international preliminary examination report is whichever of the following periods expires last: (i) 28 months from the priority date; or (ii) six months from the time provided under Rule 69.1 for the start of the international preliminary examination; or (iii) six months from the date of receipt by the International Preliminary Examining Authority of the translation furnished under Rule 55.2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'report' (Rule 70.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of Rule 70, 'report' means the international preliminary examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basis of the international preliminary examination report (Rule 70.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets the basis on which the report shall be issued: (a) if claims have been amended, the report issues on claims as amended; (b) if established as if priority had not been claimed under Rule 66.7(a) or (b), the report shall so indicate; (c) if any amendment goes beyond disclosure in the application as filed the report shall be established as if such amendment had not been made and shall indicate reasons; (c‑bis) where replacement sheets lack required letter indicating basis for amendment, report may be established as if amendment had not been made and shall indicate that; (d) if claims concern inventions without an international search report, the report shall so indicate; (e) if rectification of an obvious mistake is taken into account under Rule 66.1 the report shall so indicate (and if not taken into account pursuant to Rule 66.4bis the report shall indicate this if possible or IB shall be notified); (f) the report shall indicate the date on which a top‑up search under Rule 66.1ter was made or state that no top‑up search was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contains multiple specific procedural markers the Authority must state in the report (amendment status, priority handling, beyond‑disclosure findings, rectifications, top‑up search).

rubrics_metrics.name: Report identifications (Rule 70.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Preliminary Examining Authority which established the report shall identify itself and the international application by indicating the name of the Authority, the international application number, the name of the applicant, and the international filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates to be indicated in the report (Rule 70.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report shall indicate (i) the date on which the demand was submitted, and (ii) the date of the report (the date on which the report is completed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification in the report (Rule 70.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The report shall repeat the classification given under Rule 43.3 if the Authority agrees with it; (b) otherwise the Authority shall indicate in the report the classification, at least according to the International Patent Classification, which it considers correct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under Article 35(2) (Rule 70.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: The statement referred to in Article 35(2) shall consist of the words 'YES' or 'NO' (or equivalent) and be accompanied by the citations, explanations and observations, if any, referred to in Article 35(2). If any of the three criteria (novelty, inventive step/non‑obviousness, industrial applicability) is not satisfied the statement shall be negative; if any criterion taken separately is satisfied the report shall specify which criterion(s) are satisfied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement must be explicit and supported by citations/explanations as required by Article 35(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citations supporting Article 35(2) statements (Rule 70.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report shall cite the documents considered relevant for supporting the statements made under Article 35(2), whether or not such documents are cited in the international search report. Documents cited in the international search report need only be cited in the report when the Authority considers them relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisions of Rule 43.5(b) and (e) also apply to the report (formatting/identification of citations and bibliographic information as required by those rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanations under Article 35(2) (Rule 70.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative Instructions shall contain guidelines for when explanations referred to in Article 35(2) should or should not be given; such guidelines shall follow these principles: (i) explanations shall be given whenever the statement in relation to any claim is negative; (ii) explanations shall be given whenever the statement is positive unless the reason for citing any document is easy to imagine from the cited document; (iii) generally, explanations shall be given if the case in the last sentence of Rule 70.6(b) obtains (i.e. when some criteria are satisfied and some not).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates when narrative explanation is expected; Administrative Instructions set form/extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑written disclosures (Rule 70.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any non‑written disclosure referred to in the report shall be mentioned by indicating its kind, the date on which the written disclosure referring to it was made available to the public, and the date on which the non‑written disclosure occurred in public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of certain published documents (Rule 70.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any published application or patent referred to in the report shall be mentioned as such and accompanied by an indication of its date of publication, its filing date, and its claimed priority date (if any). The report may indicate that, in the opinion of the Authority, such claimed priority date has not been validly claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of amendments (Rule 70.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: If amendments have been made before the International Preliminary Examining Authority, this shall be indicated in the report. Where any amendment has resulted in the cancellation of an entire sheet, this fact shall also be specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mention of certain defects and other matters (Rule 70.12)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, at the time it prepares the report, the Authority considers: (i) the international application contains defects referred to in Rule 66.2(a)(iii), it shall include this opinion and reasons; (ii) the application calls for observations referred to in Rule 66.2(a)(v), it may include this opinion and must indicate reasons if it does; (iii) any situation referred to in Article 34(4) exists, it shall state this opinion and reasons; (iv) a nucleotide/amino acid sequence listing is not available in a form allowing meaningful examination, it shall so state in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remarks concerning unity of invention (Rule 70.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the applicant paid additional fees for the examination or if the application/preliminary examination was restricted under Article 34(3), the report shall so indicate. Where examination was carried out on restricted claims or on the main invention only, the report shall indicate which parts of the application were and were not the subject of international preliminary examination. The report shall contain the indications provided for in Rule 68.1 where the Authority chose not to invite the applicant to restrict claims or to pay additional fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized officer identification (Rule 70.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report shall indicate the name of the officer of the International Preliminary Examining Authority responsible for that report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and title of the report (Rule 70.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Physical requirements as to the form of the report shall be prescribed by the Administrative Instructions. (b) The report shall bear the title 'international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II of the Patent Cooperation Treaty)' together with an indication that it is established by the International Preliminary Examining Authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annexes to the report (Rule 70.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Certain replacement sheets and letters (e.g. replacement sheets under Rule 66.8, under Rule 46.5, under Rule 26.4 as applicable) and specified letters shall be annexed to the report unless superseded or reversed; (iv) where the report contains an indication under Rule 70.2(e), any sheet/letter relating to a rectification of an obvious mistake not taken into account pursuant to Rule 66.4bis shall be annexed. (b) Superseded or reversed replacement sheets and related letters shall also be annexed where (i) the Authority considers the relevant superseding/reversing amendment goes beyond the disclosure and the report contains the indication under Rule 70.2(c); or (ii) the superseding/reversing amendment lacked the required letter indicating basis and the report is established as if the amendment had not been made (Rule 70.2(c‑bis)). Superseded/reversed sheets shall be marked as provided by Administrative Instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies which replacement sheets and letters must accompany the report and when superseded/reversed sheets must nonetheless be annexed and marked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Languages of the report and annexes (Rule 70.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The report and any annex shall be in the language in which the international application is published, or, if the preliminary examination is carried out on the basis of a translation under Rule 55.2, in the language of that translation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmittal of report – recipients (Rule 71.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Preliminary Examining Authority shall, on the same day, transmit one copy of the international preliminary examination report and its annexes, if any, to the International Bureau and one copy to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Authority shall also transmit copies of other documents from the file of the international preliminary examination to the International Bureau in accordance with the Administrative Instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of cited documents; Article 36(4) requests (Rule 71.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The request under Article 36(4) may be presented any time during seven years from the international filing date. (b) The Authority may require the requesting party to pay the cost of preparing and mailing copies; cost levels are provided for in agreements between Authorities and the International Bureau. (d) Any Authority may perform these obligations through another agency responsible to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elected State may require English translation of report (Rule 72.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Any elected State may require that the international preliminary examination report established in any language other than the official language, or one of the official languages, of its national Office be translated into English. (b) Such requirement shall be notified to the International Bureau for publication in the Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of translation for the applicant (Rule 72.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall transmit a copy of the translation referred to in Rule 72.1(a) of the international preliminary examination report to the applicant at the same time as it communicates such translation to the interested elected Office(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of the written opinion of the International Searching Authority (Rule 72.2 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case referred to in Rule 73.2(b)(ii), the written opinion established by the International Searching Authority under Rule 43 bis.1 shall, upon request of the elected Office concerned, be translated into English by or under responsibility of the International Bureau. The International Bureau shall transmit a copy of the translation to the elected Office within two months from receipt of the request, and shall at the same time transmit a copy to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant's observations on translations (Rule 72.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may make written observations as to the correctness of the translation of the international preliminary examination report or of the written opinion established by the International Searching Authority under Rule 43 bis.1 and shall send a copy of the observations to each of the interested elected Offices and to the International Bureau.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparation of copies to be communicated (Rule 73.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau shall prepare the copies of the documents to be communicated under Article 36(3)(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication to elected Offices (Rule 73.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The International Bureau shall effect communication provided for in Article 36(3)(a) to each elected Office in accordance with Rule 93 bis.1 but not before the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. (b) Where the applicant makes an express request to an elected Office under Article 40(2), the International Bureau shall, upon request of that Office or the applicant: (i) if the international preliminary examination report has already been transmitted to the IB under Rule 71.1, promptly effect the communication to that Office; (ii) if the report has not been transmitted to the IB under Rule 71.1, promptly communicate a copy of the written opinion established by the ISA under Rule 43 bis.1 to that Office. (c) Where the applicant has withdrawn the demand or elections, the communication in paragraph (a) shall nevertheless be effected if the IB has received the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translations of annexes and time limit for transmittal (Rule 74.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Where an elected Office requires furnishing a translation of the international application under Article 39(1), the applicant shall within the applicable time limit transmit a translation of any replacement sheet referred to in Rule 70.16 which is annexed to the report, unless such sheet is in the language of the required translation. The same time limit applies where furnishing the translation must, because of a declaration under Article 64(2)(a)(i), be effected within the time limit applicable under Article 22. (b) Where furnishing a translation of the international application is not required by the elected Office, that Office may require the applicant to furnish, within the time limit applicable under Article 39(1), a translation into the language in which the international application was published of any replacement sheet referred to in Rule 70.16 which is annexed to the report and is not in that language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for translation of priority document (Rule 76.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant shall not be required to furnish to any elected Office a translation of the priority document before the expiration of the applicable time limit under Article 39.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of certain Rules to procedures before elected Offices (Rule 76.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules 13ter.3, 20.8(c), 22.1(g), 47.1, 49, 49bis, 49ter and 51bis shall apply to procedures before elected Offices, provided certain interpretative replacements are made (i) references to designated Office/State construed as elected Office/State; (ii) references to Articles 22/23(2)/24(2) construed as Articles 39(1)/40(2)/39(3); (iii) 'international applications filed' replaced by 'a demand submitted'; (iv) for Article 39(1) purposes, where an international preliminary examination report has been established a translation of any amendment under Article 19 is only required if that amendment is annexed to that report; (v) the reference in Rule 47.1(a) to Rule 47.4 construed as reference to Rule 61.2(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets how certain PCT rules transpose to national/elected Office proceedings and clarifies substitutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise of faculty under Article 39(1)(b) (Rule 77.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Any Contracting State allowing a time limit later than that in Article 39(1)(a) shall notify the International Bureau of the time limit so fixed. (b) Notifications shall be published in the Gazette. (c) Shortening notifications effective for demands submitted after three months from publication. (d) Lengthening notifications become effective upon publication in respect of pending or later demands, or from a later date fixed by the notifying State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit for amendment before elected Offices (Rule 78.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) The applicant shall exercise the right under Article 41 to amend claims, description and drawings before the elected Office within one month from fulfillment of Article 39(1)(a) requirements, provided that if transmittal of the international preliminary examination report under Article 36(1) has not taken place by expiration of the time limit applicable under Article 39, the applicant shall exercise that right not later than four months after such expiration. In either case, the applicant may exercise the right at any later time if permitted by national law of that State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Computation of time limits (Rule 80)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for computing periods: (80.1) years—start day after event, expire same month/day in subsequent year, with last‑day fallback if month lacks the day; (80.2) months—start day after event, expire in relevant subsequent month on same numbered day, fallback to last day if none; (80.3) days—count starts day after event and expires on last day of count; (80.4) local dates—start date is prevailing local date where event occurred; expiration date is prevailing local date where filing/payment required; (80.5) expiration on non‑working day/official holiday—period expires on next subsequent day where none of listed circumstances exist; (80.6) date of documents—interested party may prove mailing later than date borne and adjust computation; (80.7) end of working day—period expires when Office closes for business on that day though any Office may depart up to midnight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive computational rules including handling of non‑working days, local time, and documentary evidence of mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modification of time limits: proposal and decision (Rule 81)
rubrics_metrics.description: (81.1) Any Contracting State or the Director General may propose a modification under Article 47(2); proposals by States presented to Director General. (81.2) When proposal made to the Assembly, text sent to all Contracting States at least two months in advance; proposals may be amended during discussion; proposal considered adopted if none of States present votes against. (81.3) Voting by correspondence: proposal included in written communication inviting States to express vote in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Irregularities in the mail service (Rule 82.1 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party may offer evidence that he mailed a document five days prior to expiration of the time limit; except where surface mail normally arrives within two days or where no airmail available, such evidence may be offered only if mailing was by airmail and registered by postal authorities. If proven to satisfaction of the Office/organization, delay in arrival shall be excused or substitution permitted where substitute is proven identical. Evidence and substitute must be submitted within one month after the date the interested party noticed (or should have noticed) the delay/loss and in no case later than six months after expiration of the time limit. National Offices/organizations which notify IB that they will do so shall apply these provisions where a delivery service other than postal authorities is used, with recording requirements; notification published in Gazette. Any Office/organization may apply these provisions even if delivery service used was not specified in notification or no notification sent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies strict evidentiary and procedural conditions for excusing delay or replacing lost documents; registered/recorded mailing is central.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse by designated or elected State of delays in meeting time limits (Rule 82 bis)
rubrics_metrics.description: (82 bis.1) 'Time limit' in Article 48(2) includes any time limit fixed in the Treaty/Regulations and any time limit fixed by receiving Office, Authorities, IB or applicable by receiving Office under national law. (82 bis.2) The provisions of the national law referred to in Article 48(2) concerning excusing delay (reinstatement of rights, restoration, restitutio in integrum, further processing, extension of time limits) are those applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines scope of 'time limit' and ties excuse/reinstatement to national law provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of errors by the Receiving Office or International Bureau (Rule 82 ter)
rubrics_metrics.description: (82 ter.1) If applicant proves to satisfaction of any designated/elected Office that the international filing date is incorrect due to error by the receiving Office or that the priority claim was erroneously considered void by the receiving Office or IB, and if the error is such that the Office would rectify it under national law/practice, the Office shall rectify the error and treat the application as if accorded the rectified filing date or as if the priority claim had not been considered void. (Paragraphs (b)–(d) cover cases where filing date was accorded on basis of incorporation by reference and set out procedures for treating the application, giving the applicant opportunity to make observations, and allowing applicant to request that missing parts be disregarded for national processing.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives procedures and applicant rights when filing‑date/priority errors attributable to receiving Office/IB are alleged; requires opportunity to make observations before certain corrective treatments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excuse of delay in meeting time limits and extension due to disruptions (Rule 82 quater)
rubrics_metrics.description: (82 quater.1) Any interested party may offer evidence that a time limit was not met due to war, revolution, civil disorder, strike, natural calamity, epidemic, general unavailability of electronic communications services or other like reason in the locality where the party resides/has business/is staying, and that the relevant action was taken as soon as reasonably possible. Such evidence must be addressed to the Office/Authority/IB not later than six months after expiration of the time limit; if proven, delay shall be excused. The excuse need not be taken into account by any designated/elected Office before which the applicant has already performed the acts referred to in Article 22 or 39. The need for evidence may be waived by the Office/Authority/IB under published conditions, in which case a statement by the interested party must be submitted. (82 quater.2) Any national Office may provide that where a time limit is not met due to unavailability of permitted electronic means at that Office, delay shall be excused provided the action was performed on the next working day when electronic means were available; the Office shall publish information on the unavailability. (82 quater.3) provides for extension of time limits due to general disruption (title present).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines acceptable causes for excusing delay, strict deadlines for submitting evidence/statement (six months), and procedures for electronic‑service outages; Offices may publish waivers/criteria.
